title: U.S. House · Maryland's 2nd District
area: Much of Baltimore County and Carroll County, along with parts of Baltimore City.

context.text: Incumbent John Olszewski Jr. defeated Clint Spellman Jr. in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Dave Wallace defeated Nnabu Eze in the Republican primary; former candidate Kim Klacik did not make the ballot.

summary.text: John Olszewski Jr. is the Democratic incumbent in Maryland's 2nd Congressional District. A former Baltimore County public school teacher, he served in the Maryland House of Delegates and as Baltimore County Executive before being sworn into Congress in January 2025. He is seeking a second term.

background.text: Born in Baltimore, Maryland, in 1982. According to his congressional website, he is a product of Maryland's public schools and a first-generation college graduate.

Earned a bachelor's degree from Goucher College in 2004, a master's degree from George Washington University in 2005, and a Ph.D. in public policy from the University of Maryland-Baltimore County in 2017.

Began his career as a teacher in the Baltimore County Public Schools system. Ballotpedia also lists work as a senior manager of legislative affairs for the City of Baltimore and as a software executive at SAS.
Served in the Maryland House of Delegates for more than nine years, and according to his congressional website was the youngest lawmaker to chair Baltimore County's House delegation.

Elected Baltimore County Executive twice, leading Maryland's third-largest jurisdiction, with a $5 billion budget and more than 9,000 employees. His congressional website cites the county's near-universal free community college program, its first public campaign finance system, and an Office of the Inspector General among his administration's initiatives.
Sworn into Congress in January 2025. Serves on the Small Business and Foreign Affairs Committees and on the Democratic Steering and Policy Committee.
Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 84.5% of the vote over Clint Spellman Jr.
According to his congressional website, he lives in eastern Baltimore County with his wife, Marisa, and their daughter.

priorities.text: Expanding workforce development and enhancing education and housing access.
Defending the foundations of American democracy.

positions.summary: Voted for bipartisan legislation to extend expiring Affordable Care Act tax credits for 22 million Americans, after previously voting against a Republican bill he said failed to address rising premiums.
positions.quote: No American should ever have to worry about whether or not they can afford to see a doctor when they are sick.

positions.summary: Voted against funding for ICE operations without new accountability measures, citing wrongful arrests and deportations of U.S. citizens, and called for reforms such as banning the detention of U.S. citizens and requiring body-worn cameras before he would support DHS/ICE funding.
positions.quote: As Americans, it is time that we say ‘enough’ to ICE – which is why I will again vote no on legislation that funds its operations without any new accountability measures.

positions.summary: Campaign priorities page says he insists on immediate, bold action on climate change and backs large-scale investment in renewable energy to cut carbon emissions.
positions.quote: Johnny O backs strategic, large-scale investments in renewable energy: deploying solar, wind and other clean-energy technologies not only to dramatically cut carbon emissions

positions.summary: Campaign priorities page says he is pushing to end the Trump-era tariffs, citing higher prices.
positions.quote: He’s pushing to extend critical health-insurance tax credits, end the reckless Trump-era tariffs that are driving up prices

positions.summary: Campaign priorities page criticizes Trump Administration policies that divert taxpayer dollars to private schools and says he is pushing back.
positions.quote: The Trump Administration is pushing policies that ban books, enable discrimination against LGBTQ+ students, and divert taxpayer dollars to private schools.

record.text: As a member of the Maryland House of Delegates, championed earned sick leave legislation and a minimum wage increase.
Cast a vote in the Maryland Senate delegation vote that secured marriage equality in Maryland.

As Baltimore County Executive, launched a near-universal free community college program for county residents and created the county's first public campaign finance system and Office of the Inspector General.
Serves on the House Small Business Committee and House Foreign Affairs Committee for the 2025-2026 term.

candidates.name: Dave Wallace

summary.text: Dave Wallace is the Republican nominee for Maryland's 2nd Congressional District and owns a kitchen wholesale business. A former NIH cancer researcher, he has sought office repeatedly since 2010, including this seat in 2022 and 2024, and won the June 23, 2026 Republican primary.

background.text: Graduated from South Carroll High School and earned a B.S. in biology from Salisbury University.
Worked in immunological cancer research at the National Institutes of Health before founding Chesapeake Kitchen Wholesalers in 1981; Ballotpedia says he still owns the business.
Founded the organization Restore America's Mission in 2008.

Ran as a Republican for the Maryland House of Delegates (District 5A) in 2010, and for Maryland's 8th Congressional District in 2012 (finishing second in the Republican primary) and 2014 (the Republican nominee, losing the general election to Chris Van Hollen, 39.6% to 60.2%).
Ran in the 2016 Republican primary for U.S. Senate in Maryland, receiving 6.1% of the vote.
Finished second in the 2022 Republican primary for Maryland's 2nd District (20.2%) and second in the 2024 primary (23.5%, behind Kim Klacik).
Won the June 23, 2026 Republican primary with 88.9% of the vote over Nnabu Eze.
According to Ballotpedia, he has been married to his wife, Barbara, for more than thirty years and has three children.

priorities.text: Protecting medical freedom: his campaign site lists it as an issue, and his 2024 campaign site described it as the right to choose whether to wear a mask or take COVID vaccines.
Fighting government corruption, including support for term limits and a presidential one-line budget veto.
Protecting police and other first responders with resources and equipment.

statements.quote: Dave Wallace will protect the police and other first responders. He will vote to give them the resources and equipment they need to protect us from criminals both foreign and domestic.
He will vote for the use of energy sources wherever they happen to be, including natural gas in Maryland.

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website read in full (it carries the same issue text Ballotpedia quoted from 2024). No Ballotpedia survey, questionnaire or debate answers found; no stance on the other guide issues was found.
